subject: Documentation checklist for wholesale tax-exempt coverage (states & next steps)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Documentation checklist for wholesale tax-exempt coverage (states & next steps)

Hi Alex —

Great talking earlier. To unblock invoices and ensure we apply wholesale tax-exempt pricing correctly, we need a few items from Legacy Retail. State rules vary so we want to collect the minimal acceptable evidence that our billing team can validate without tying your finance team up for days.

Please provide the following (attach as PDFs where possible):

1) A signed resale/certificate of exemption covering the ship-to states where you claim exemption; the document should include the purchaser name, the ship-to address, and the seller name (Redwood Inference or Redwood Inference, Inc.)
2) If you claim blanket/blanket-like coverage for multiple states, either a multi-state blanket certificate or a state-specific affidavit for states that do not accept blanket forms (Ohio, Pennsylvania, etc.). We have an Ohio affidavit template attached.
3) The EIN/Tax ID for the purchasing entity as it appears on the certificate.
4) If the certificate is signed by an agent, include a short authorization letter or POA showing signatory authority.
5) A contact for purchase-order invoicing and a preferred billing email for our accounts receivable.

I've attached: 1) a Redwood resale-certificate template (redwood_resale_template.pdf) you can fill and sign, and 2) an Ohio affidavit sample if you need a state-specific form.

If you can return the signed certificate and any supporting affidavits by next Friday (17 Sep), we can lift the tax hold and issue corrected invoices for the prior two shipments back to 01-Aug-2026. If you prefer, we can send a DocuSign envelope — I can prepare that and include the exact seller legal name.

Thanks — simple checklist to reduce back-and-forth. Happy to hop on a quick 15-min call if helpful.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Alex —

Appreciate the quick response and the DocuSign links. Answers inline below and next steps: 

- NY/NJ certificate: yes, that will work if the purchaser name and EIN match the invoices Redwood has on file. If the certificate lists DBAs, please include a short cover note that ties the DBA to the purchasing legal entity (a one-line statement or the EIN is sufficient).
- Ohio (3PL): the attached Ohio affidavit is acceptable for shipments handled by a 3PL as long as the affidavit references the purchasing entity and lists the ship-to states or ship-to address range. If your 3PL operates from multiple ship-to locations in OH, include the full list or provide a statement that covers all OH ship-to addresses your account uses.
- PO stamping: a signed PDF with the PO number added is fine for our billing team; agent signature rules only kick in if someone other than the purchasing entity signs the certificate. If an agent signs, include the POA/authorization memo.

Next steps I will take after receipt: 
1) Our billing team (cc: Ben) will validate the documents against our seller name and EIN on file. If everything matches, we'll reprocess invoices for 2026-08-01 through 2026-09-01 as tax-exempt and issue corrected invoices within 5 business days.
2) If small gaps exist (missing EIN, unclear DBA mapping), we'll request a one-line clarification via email to avoid another round of signatures.
3) If you want, I can prepare a DocuSign envelope pre-filled with Redwood's legal seller name to speed signature collection — say the word and I'll send it.

Ben/Naomi — FYI for validation queue.

Thanks again — we aim to minimize billing disruption.

—
Soojin
